final.body:
The account is a pure fold from a multiset of immutable event records to a snapshot; delivery multiplicity and order never enter the result except through the reducer's idempotence and the reducer's choice of latest revision.

Mechanism. (1) Deduplicate deliveries structurally: each record is immutable and a booking/revision pair has at most one content, so duplicates collapse via structural equality. unique preserves first-occurrence order but only membership matters here, since order is discarded next. (2) Group surviving records by booking. (3) For each booking reduce its records by max revision: revision is an integer and a strictly higher revision supersedes ALL lower revisions, so max_by(revision) yields exactly the latest event regardless of arrival sequence. Uniqueness of content per (booking,revision) makes this deterministic. (4) Classify the latest event: if kind == release, the booking reserves 0; if kind == hold, it reserves its quantity exactly when expires_at > now and 0 otherwise. Quantity is the absolute quantity of that booking version, never a delta, so no accumulation is needed and no subtraction can corrupt it. (5) Union the latest events' item names with all stock item names, sort ascending, and for each item sum the active latest quantities (sum over the empty set is 0) and emit {"item":NAME,"reserved":TOTAL,"available":CAPACITY-TOTAL}. Stock items with no events naturally get reserved 0 and available = capacity.

Why replay, reordering, expiry, and cancellation interact correctly. Replay: the dedup step is idempotent, so any finite number of redeliveries yields the same surviving set. Reordering: the only order-sensitive step is selecting the latest revision; max revision is a commutative, associative, total reduction, so input order is irrelevant, and delivery order never appears in the output. Expiry: expiry is decided by comparing the latest event's expires_at to input.now, not by which records arrived; an expired latest hold contributes 0 and, crucially, does not resurrect an older unexpired hold, because older revisions were already superseded before expiry was evaluated. Cancellation: a later revision of kind release supersedes earlier holds and reserves 0; it does not delete the booking, so no rejection ordering is invented, no booking is silently discarded, and the released quantity simply frees capacity. Oversubscription is never clamped: if the sum of active latest quantities exceeds capacity, available is capacity - total and may be negative, which the arithmetic expresses directly.

Assumptions. Revisions, quantities, capacities, and now are integers; a booking has one immutable item; a (booking,revision) pair has a single content; every event item is a listed stock item; revision comparison is meaningful across all events of one booking. If any of these fail (e.g. two contents for one booking/revision, a non-listed item, or a fractional quantity), the fold is undefined and execution failure is the honest outcome.

Falsifiers. The account is defeated by: (a) two records sharing a (booking,revision) with different quantity/kind/item; (b) a latest release still contributing quantity; (c) an expired latest hold allowing an older unexpired hold to reappear; (d) a duplicate delivery changing reserved; (e) delivery order changing the output; (f) available being clamped at zero under oversubscription; (g) omitting a stock item with no events. Any one of these observed would falsify the account.

What a revision preserves. A higher revision preserves the booking's identity and supersession semantics: it replaces all lower revisions while preserving the property that exactly one latest event determines the booking's contribution, and it preserves the invariant that lower revisions never influence the snapshot. Successful behavior that any change must keep: idempotence under replay, order-independence, expiry evaluated only on the latest hold, cancellation as full supersession to zero, unclamped negative availability, and inclusion of event-free stock items sorted by name.
